## Verdict: PASS. The failing line is fixed, and there is no new blocker

## (1) The failing line, re-run

The line is N-53 (5): "bridgeGaps re-reads X/Y per iteration (hygiene; no test shift)". Each part of its required
change was checked.

* **Every capture-then-allocate site in the five files is gone. CONFIRMED by reading all five files whole.**
  * `winding.ts` (739 lines). Only `buildOverlay` and `bridgeGaps` allocate, through `insertChain`. `buildOverlay`
    holds no table or column across its insertions. `bridgeGaps` now takes `p.vertices.x` and `.y` inside each gap's
    pass, after the previous pass's `insertChain`, and builds both bridge points before its own `insertChain`. It
    holds `p = tx.plat` across passes, but that is the arena object, not a table. Its `starts`, `ends`, `segments` and
    `walk.steps` are plain JS arrays. `orientSegments`, `pathFlow`, `shortestPath`, `glueWalks`, `balanceFlow`,
    `windingLabels` and `traceKept` take `origin`, `next`, `x` and `y` only after the overlay's last insertion, and
    none of them allocates. They call only `handleOf`, `rowsOn`, `faceWalk`, `isHalfEdgeLive` and `isFaceLive`.
    `handleOf` was read in `arena/rows.ts` and `arena/handles.ts`: it is a lookup that "never interns", so it does
    not grow the handle table.
  * `booleans.ts` (46 lines), `buffer.ts` (399), `offsetFace.ts` (108) and `insetRing.ts` (149) hold no arena table
    or column at all. They read faces through `faceRings` and build only through `overlayRegion`. This matches
    C-0293 (2).
* **The pin exists and kills the fault. CONFIRMED.**
  * `packages/kernel/test/arr/booleans-buffers/growth.test.ts` uses M0-a-02's tiny-tables switch (`setTinyTables`
    from `src/arena/debug.ts`, which is in the tree), plus a `vi.mock` of the arena barrel that poisons every vertex
    table a growth replaces.
  * The seat's targeted mutants of `bridgeGaps` were each run on `growth.test.ts` together with the seat's control
    (described below):

    | mutant | change | `growth.test.ts` |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | M1 | the pre-fix file: X and Y captured once at entry | killed ("two bridges in one ring …") |
    | M2 | X and Y captured once per walk | killed |
    | M3 | gap test fresh, both bridge points from the entry capture | killed |
    | M4 | X fresh, Y from the entry capture | killed |
    | M5 | only the far end `b` from the entry capture | killed |
    | M6 | the gap test from the entry capture, the points fresh | killed |
    | M7 | the bridge not spliced into `walk.steps` (not an N-53 promise) | survives; see note 28 |

  * Control `zz-nc-unpoisoned.test.ts` was `growth.test.ts` with the poison disarmed and `replaced` expected to be 0,
    so it used tiny tables only. It was green on the fixed code and on M1 – M6. So with tiny tables alone, the dead
    copy still holds the right coordinates, and the pre-fix code was correct but latent, as N-53 and C-0293 (3) say.
    Only the poison makes the stale read observable. A first version of the control failed on its own copied
    `replaced > 0` line; it was corrected before the runs used here.
* **The choices row exists. CONFIRMED.** C-0293 names N-53 (4) and (5), the re-read rule, the audit, the pin and the
  before/after comparison. It is in the landed record's appends.
* **There is no test shift. CONFIRMED, on a seed of the seat's own.** Both of the item's test folders were run at
  `PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=1000`, `PLAT_FUZZ_SEED=9311`, with `PLAT_FUZZ_COUNTS` and `PLAT_REFUSALS_OUT` set, once on the fixed
  tree and once on the pre-fix twin in `m1`:
  * `PLAT_FUZZ_COUNTS`: byte-equal after sorting (19 lines).
  * `PLAT_REFUSALS_OUT`: byte-equal after sorting (95 lines).
  * Test outcomes: equal except one. The pin "two bridges in one ring, the vertex table grown between them" is red
    on the pre-fix twin (`Tests 1 failed | 184 passed (185)`; the failed-test list holds that one line) and green on
    the fixed tree (`Tests 185 passed (185)`). Every other test, golden and hand result of both folders passes on
    both sides.
  * The tallies, for example: offsetFace drawn 995, insertChain refusals 4, own 0; buffer drawn 989, insertChain 11,
    own 0; insetRing 948 drawn, 0 refused; the four boolean operations 1 000 drawn each, 0 refused; 0 failures in
    every verdict.
* **With tiny tables everywhere, the outputs are the same. CONFIRMED.** Mirror `m2` set the kernel's tiny-tables
  switch on by default (`let tiny = true` in `src/arena/debug.ts`, in the mirror only). Every arena of every test in
  both folders, including the scratch overlays and the testkit agreement harness, then started at capacity 1 and
  replaced a table on every allocation. At seed 9311 × 1 000 the result was `Tests 185 passed (185)`, with
  `PLAT_FUZZ_COUNTS` (19 lines) and `PLAT_REFUSALS_OUT` (95 lines) byte-equal to the default-size run on the tree.
  So no other read of the item's five files goes stale or off the end of a table under constant growth.
  * One limit: this probe would not catch a stale read whose dead copy still holds equal values. The poisoned pin
    covers that for `bridgeGaps`, and the reading audit above covers the rest.
